query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic phases during solidification and exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence. Under rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating assessed by thermal analysis, what single intervention could increase amorphous retention and thermal stability while overcoming extensive primary crystallization? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the alloy’s reported glass formation and crystallization behavior, the relevant cooling-rate and reheating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Minor boron micro-alloying (≈2 at.% B substituted for Mn in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20) will increase the glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the alloy, suppressing the extensive primary crystallization that occurs during solidification and on reheating.
generation.material_initial_state: Molten equiatomic Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy at 50–100 K superheat above its liquidus, held under an inert atmosphere before quenching.
generation.intervention: Add 2 at.% B (replacing an equal total atomic percentage of Mn) and process the melt identically (melt-spinning, wheel speeds giving 10²–10⁴ K s⁻¹; DSC at 20 K min⁻¹).
generation.conditions: Inert Ar atmosphere, ambient pressure; cooling rates 10²–10⁴ K s⁻¹ during melt-spinning; reheating at 20 K min⁻¹ in DSC.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron increases chemical and topological disorder, promoting icosahedral/short-range order in the undercooled liquid and raising the liquid viscosity.
generation.mechanism: B forms strong, covalent-like bonds with transition metals and P, lowering the liquidus temperature and increasing the thermodynamic and kinetic barriers for nucleation of the FCC high-entropy solid solution and M3P-type phosphides. This delays the multistep primary crystallization cascade, allowing more of the melt to bypass crystallization and vitrify; the same bonding raises the activation energy for atomic rearrangement on reheating, increasing Tx.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline alloy: 1) The critical cooling rate for obtaining ≥90 % amorphous fraction will drop by ≥1 order of magnitude (≈10⁴ K s⁻¹ → ≈10³ K s⁻¹). 2) Melt-spun ribbons quenched at ≥10⁴ K s⁻¹ will be fully amorphous (>95 %) instead of partly crystalline. 3) The first crystallization onset temperature (Tx) in DSC will increase by 20 ± 10 K, widening ΔTx and indicating higher thermal stability.
generation.baseline: Without B, the alloy retains only partial amorphous structure at 10⁴ K s⁻¹ and begins crystallizing through multiple primary phases at Tx ≈ 580–600 K during 20 K min⁻¹ reheating.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect holds for 0.5–4 at.% B and cooling rates ≥10³ K s⁻¹. At slower quench rates (<10² K s⁻¹) or B contents ≥5 at.% the alloy still crystallizes primarily or forms B-rich intermetallics, negating the improvement.
generation.uncertainty: Exact shifts in Tx and critical cooling rate are estimated; interaction of B with high P levels may introduce unforeseen compounds. No direct experimental data for this specific composition is yet available.

falsification_experiment.design: Cast two alloys: (i) Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 (baseline) and (ii) Cr16Mn15Fe16Co16Ni16P20B2. Produce melt-spun ribbons at wheel surface velocities giving ~10², 10³ and 10⁴ K s⁻¹. Characterize each condition.
measurements: X-ray diffraction (Cu Kα) to quantify amorphous fraction via peak deconvolution
Differential scanning calorimetry at 20 K min⁻¹ to obtain Tg and Tx
Optical/SEM imaging to verify primary phase suppression
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the B-doped alloy fails to show BOTH (a) ≥20 K increase in Tx AND (b) ≥50 % reduction in the critical cooling rate required for ≥90 % amorphous fraction, compared with the baseline alloy, under otherwise identical processing.
